title: Model Supply Pulse: Short-Window Availability Forecast & Procurement Signals
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight, production-ready short-window (1-7 day) availability forecasting pipeline for models and a procurement signal layer that recommends actions when supply risk rises. This ticket scopes the product work: hypothesis, data inputs, dashboard and alerting UX, success metrics, and a minimal runbook for SRE/procurement handoff.
objective: Give GTM, procurement and SRE teams an actionable early-warning signal for imminent model availability degradation so we can pre-provision alternatives or negotiate capacity before customers are impacted.
hypotheses: A 1-7 day forecast combining provider telemetry (rate-limit trends, error spikes), regional capacity signals, and historical outage patterns will predict short-window availability drops with >= 80% precision for actionable windows (3 days).

Thresholded signals (e.g., predicted capacity drop >25% for a critical model in a region) will reduce customer-impacting failovers by enabling preemptive provisioning on Dedicated nodes or routing to verified fallback variants.
A compact UI with clear recommended actions and confidence bands will increase cross-functional adoption versus raw telemetry feeds.
data_sources: Host telemetry: 5xx/429 rates per model-region (hosted API logs)
Routing & capacity: Dedicated pool utilization and quota churn events
External: vendor status feeds, marketplace announcements
Historical incident dataset (past 18 months): outage start/stop, root cause tags
Synthetic probe results: periodic RPS/latency probes to candidate model endpoints
Billing/price-change events (to detect sudden cost-based throttles)
approach: Phase 1 (MVP): build a signal fusion pipeline that ingests daily and near-real-time metrics, computes short-window forecasts using an exponential smoothing baseline plus anomaly detection, surfaces probability bands and a discrete procurement action recommendation. Deliverables: single-dashboard view (per-model, per-region), webhook alerts, and a procurement runbook mapping signals to actions. Phase 2: add ML ensemble forecasting, backtesting harness, and integration with Reserved Capacity planner.
metrics: Time from alert to accepted mitigation (procurement/SRE) <= 48h for high-confidence alerts
Reduction in customer-facing failovers for alerted incidents (pilot cohort) >= 30%
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end pipeline ingests telemetry and emits a probability forecast for model availability for a 1-7 day horizon
Dashboard shows per-model/per-region forecast with confidence band and recommended action
Webhook or Slack alert delivers procurement recommendation when configured thresholds are met
A short runbook (<= 2 pages) maps alerts to concrete actions (reserve burst, promote fallback model, open vendor channel)
Pilot run with two high-usage models in US-West and EU-West for at least 14 production days and backtested accuracy documented
